project_name: South Sioux City Data Center Park
developer: City of South Sioux City / Community Development Agency
status_detail: Speculative data-center park land effort did not produce required jobs; city agenda described 108 acres acquired from a 314-acre parcel with CDBG funds for a speculative data park, and Nebraska DED later said the 100-acre park originally created for a large data center was converted to light industrial use.
notes: County EDA page links a rural economic development strategic plan; official city and Nebraska DED records show the data-center park concept was historical/speculative and later repurposed, not an operating hyperscale facility.

project_name: Fremont Technology Park data center recruitment area
status_detail: City planning commission study-session minutes described rezoning about 80 acres from agricultural/urban reserve to limited industrial for a city-owned Technology Park, with officials recruiting software users on the east end and data centers on the west/center portion; no tenant or completion evidence found.
notes: Dodge County agendas include Northeast Nebraska Economic Development District ROI references to 'Data Center - Land Acquisition'; this appears to be a historical/speculative recruitment site rather than a confirmed operating data center.

status_detail: Google lists Omaha as a Nebraska data-center community; City of Omaha/news reports identify the campus near State Street and Blair High Road, announced as part of more than $750M Nebraska investment. Third-party trackers conflict on capacity and status, so capacity left null.
notes: Local reporting places the Omaha campus in Douglas County near State Street and Blair High Road; Google official page confirms Omaha as one of its Nebraska data-center communities.

status_detail: Operator website describes the 1623 Farnam Street Omaha facility as a flagship network-neutral edge interconnection hub with Omaha IX, cloud on-ramps, 50+ carriers, and an expanding Omaha campus; USDataMap lists it as operational with 12 MW.
notes: Capacity comes from tracker; operational existence and Omaha address are from operator pages.

status_detail: HDR project page says the Omaha Douglas Public Building Commission renovated sublevel C to consolidate data servers into a secure data center environment with N+1 reliability and 24/7 operation; size listed as 20,000 sf.
notes: Public-sector/civic data center, not hyperscale; included under broad county exploration because it is a named local data-center project.
